text: "Zombimon: Digital Arena" — The board shows a tournament bracket. Each player raises a Zombimon from egg to mega. First to knock out all opponent's forms wins.
The rulebook says the game takes 45-60 minutes. Yours always end in 20 because someone rage-quits.
The spinner is shaped like a Zombivice. Six sides: Feed, Train, Battle, Rest, Evolve, and — the dreaded — Sick.
There's a variant rule called "Apocalypse Mode" where every space is a battle. The author clearly designed this alone.
You unfold the board. The artwork traces a Zombimon's journey from a digital egg in a lab to a mega-form reigning over a wasteland.
You flip through the deck. The holographic Plantborgmon catches the light — it's the rarest card in the set.
There's a Kremata with 3000 ATK. Underneath the stats it says "It dreams of becoming a deadly creature." Profound.
The rulebook explains Evolution mechanics: sacrifice one monster to summon a stronger form from your hand. Just like the real digivice!
You find a misprint card where Shriekermon's name is spelled "Shreikermon." Probably worth something to a collector.
The back of each card has the Zombimon logo and a URL to a website that hasn't existed since 2023.
You sort the cards by type. You have 12 plant monsters, 8 shadow types, and way too many basic egg cards.
You pose the Shoggothmon action figure in a dramatic stance in your hand. It wobbles slightly, then tips over.
You carefully pose the figure's limbs into a flying kick. The articulation is surprisingly smooth.
You strike a battle pose with the figure. It looks way cooler on the packaging.
"PLANTBORGMON, USE VINE WHIP!" Nothing happens, but it felt good to say it.
You hold the action figure up and admire the sculpt. The detail on the carapace is incredible.
The action figure has 14 points of articulation. You spend way too long posing each joint.
You study the box. The puzzle claimed to include all 27 lineages, but you've found at least 29 distinct monster forms in the pieces.
There's a piece shaped like a Sproutmon's head. You've been trying to find where it goes for the past hour.
The completed puzzle image on the box shows a beautiful evolution tree. You'll never finish it.
You sort pieces by color. Green pieces are Sproutmon leaves. Blue are water types. Black is the void where your will to live goes.
You find two pieces that fit together perfectly. The satisfaction is immesurable.
